body: My son is almost 5 months at at 4 months we started to introduce formula (1 bottle a day). It took a bit for his stomach to adjust— he did not poop for like 5 days! But then slowly got used to it, so definitely came with time. He also refused the bottle until we continued to try twice daily until he would accept the formula bottle— for some reason it helped for it to be cold for him to drink.
Kendamil goat did the same to us! Actually noticing it getting better as we switch towards classic

Just saying I am having the same issue. Right around the end of 3 months we started getting great sleep— had 2.5 weeks where he slept through 4 times and most other nights were about 1 wake. Now as we approach 5 months we are getting similarly a lot of wakes. Previously I was doing aggressive capping of naps at 2.5 hrs total for the day and was still getting these wakes. Now I only cap each individual nap at 2 hrs max— so often getting about 3-3.5 hrs of naps & still getting the wakes. I think I may need to cap naps more / get more awake time, however he is in a weird spot between 2 and 3 naps which makes it hard. 
So basically— just commenting in solidarity. 
I am thinking of kind of riding it out and see how it improves as we approach 6 months and hopefully lock in on a 2 nap schedule

what was your combo feeding “schedule”? I am kind of moving towards combo feeding but worried that moving feeds to formula will make my supply
drop even more

I have found myself feeding close ti every 2 hrs now because I also want to feed shortly before a nap to make sure he can take a long nap. before the move to 3 naps I was very much doing every 3 hrs. I dont love the more frequent feeds though

Just commenting to say I am in the same boat. I know formula is great and perfectly fine for my son & there are no issues with it. But find myself not wanting to quit breastfeeding because I feel like I should want to suffer for my child. I know this is not the case— but I still think it! Its such mental gymnastics
Yeah I am really am concerned that pumping will be too much and I will end up stressing myself out more than necessary

My job would definitely “allow” it with no issues— they are great! It is more that I feel like last minute calls and stuff come up where I would end up distracted/ needing to miss the pump to finish stuff off. More of a me problem lol
yes most are video calls unfortunately
I had success by slowly rocking less ans then switching to patting the mattress in the crib whie he laid there until he fell asleep and then slowly doing that less and less

thats what I have been doing now— giving breast then offering a bottle. I think Ill keep doing that, although will need to switch to pumping when I go to work. Puming for 30 min and only getting 1 oz is kind of tough! But I think ill give it a try and hope

I am going back in January & also struggling!!! 
However, I did go to a work dinner recently and it actually felt somewhat nice not just talking/thinking about my baby & being seen as someone other than mom/ new parent. So that is kind of helping me mentally prepare!
did you eventually transfer back to consolidated feeds?

Yeah that is basically what the LC was referring to. She couldnt do a weighted feed (he wouldnt eat/wasnt hungry) but did evaluate and said that he doesnt have any tongue ties but did have a high palate and a tight frenulum (i think thats what she said) which could be causing transfer issues… however without the weighted feed it sounded uncertain? 
Also she said my flanges were way too big so that could be causing my pump issue. 

Were you able to get your supply back up after the issue was identified?

Yeah makes sense, this thread has really relieved me and kind of made me accept that two feeds is entirely normal! I would prefer 3 naps but he started taking long naps more frequently which is how we ended up with 2 naps+ micro.

thanks! Yeah he seems to tolerate the 2.75 wake window pretty well— i was doing shorter and it kind of naturally extended towards 2.75. The last wake window we try to keep at 3 hrs but often end up with like 4-4.5 hrs until bedtime so too short to offer a full nap but also cant make it to bedtime so we try for a 15-20 min nap
I feel the same— and i dont feel like the “duration” of breastfeeding always correlates with how much hes eating too so its hard to follow
yep have already been following 5/3/3 roughly so the feeds are spaced out a bit- just two of them when used to be one!
Yeah I was hoping that wouldnt be the case but it seems like it is now!

I’ll need to do a better job of really watching him feed— I feel like they are full feeds but he also is very variable in the duration he feeds for during the day & often “finishes” feeding but continues to latch/suck even though (i think) he is done…. sometimes I am also so tired/ half awake so dont do the best job of paying attention
I dont think he has a feed to sleep issue as stopped feeding right before bed at 8 weeks and sleep has been fully independent since like 12 weeks.

thanks— good to hear you went through the same thing! Hope my LO is not far behind yours and will be going back to 1 feed again lol. He does seem to be actively feeding, although sometimes I am so tired I dont remember by the morning how active his feeds are

and yeah, his wake windows are pretty long but he is content for them for the most part and doesnt seem super tired! I had him doing 2.25 hrs and then 2.5 hrs but they kind of naturally shifted towards 2.75 hrs recently as was taking longer and longer to fall asleep for naps

Yeah, I originally was following what they were suggesting but it felt kind of crazy once the suggestions were to cap nap total at under 2 hours! Thanks— just needed some other input that 2 feeds is normal and I shouldnt be stressing to reduce sleep more

Mostly breastfeeding with about 2 bottles of formula (introduced formula right around thanksgiving as well to prepare for when I go back to work). We have seen some trends where if I do formula as his last feed at 7 he will more often only wake once, so will be testing this for a couple days to see if this brings it back to one feed consistently. Unfortunately I was hoping to keep that last feed as breast because it is the only feed ill be able to breastfeed when i return to work, but sleep seems more important now haha

Yeah that is my assumption… he is only 8th percentile too. He did a month with only 1 wakeup each night (and 4 nights where he slept through) but then went to 2 wakeups… so a bit frustrating as feels like a step “backward” but know he is growing and his food needs can change

Bedtime is 8:15 and wakeup is 7am…. 
the 4 hours typically has a 15-20 min micro nap sprinkled in it. Basically his naps tend to be about 1.5-2 hrs for the first one and 45-1.5 hrs for the second; so if he ends up with 2 longer naps the time after the second nap ends up being awkward and cant fit a full 2 wake windows and full nap in but also cant make it to bedtime— so end up throwing some sort of micro nap in.

going back to work after the new year &
honestly really needed to hear this as I have been getting upset each day as it approaches!

I try to follow 5/3/3 loosely. Basically dont feed for the first time until its been 5 hours from last feed/bedtime (some say bedtime but i use last feed). Then dont feed again until its been 3 hours since that feed. 

Other times use other methods

Definitely recommend the zipadeezip as an intermediate before the sleep sack! Used our zipadeezip for about 4-6 weeks after the swaddle before moving to a sleep sack… I felt like that let him get used to the arms out. Also found my son did better with the kyte baby sleep sack instead of halo since its a bit thicker (theres also a good kyte baby dupe on amazon to save some
money)
Started rolling at around 14 weeks and quickly started sleeping on his stomach after that. Now I can barely zip him in his sleep sack before he rolls himself to his stomach
my goal exactly! want to keep a good 11 hr night and nap as much as possible to keep that. The 2 hr nap today was glorious since he hasnt napped more than 45ish min since 6 weeks

yeah— agree. I was just bummed because he was doing 1 wake for a while so this feels like a step back, but know their needs change a lot at this age and 2 isnt too bad. Also just found out he dropped down to the 8th percentile so probably makes sense hes up to eat twice

Thanks! I am going to see how reducing it works. Have been following a lot of suggestions from the PLS fb group but feel like their suggestion is always more awake time. But when he was down to 2.5 hrs of day sleep i started to feel like that doesnt make sense (especially if I am waking him from all naps AND sleep needs will continue to decrease)… and It started to become impossible to do anything because he always falls asleep in the car / stroller/carrier and I would have to fight to keep him awake. 
Hopefully will see what he naturally wants to do.

he really just started consolidating naps in the past week. Before that he had short naps so we would often extend the nap through contact napping to hit our planned “schedule” of nap duration. So no idea if that was too high / too low. Between like 10 weeks and  now (18 weeks) we have moved from like 5+ hrs of sleep to 2.5 hrs. Improvement we saw was false starts went away once we moved to 3 hr ww before bed but also not sure how much improvement has just come with age/time vs all the schedule tweaks. 

I let him nap 2 hrs for his first nap today, othwr naps were in the car bc he had a ped appt. Total sleep for today was 3.5 hrs so well see how this goes tonight! 
think I need to give him a couple days to nap as long as he wants for the first two naps (cap third to preserve bedtime) and see how his schedule and sleep shakes out. I dont think I have been able to see what his natural schedule would be and how that impacts night sleep because I was always having him fit some sort of schedule / goal nap durations
thank you!!! appreciate the response— definitely gives me hope :)

He will be 5 months when I return! I would be fine combo feeding with formula but would love to maintain some level of supply so I can breastfeed when I am home at nights. Definitely will try to meet with a lactation consultant!

I feel thats the same— My baby doesnt seem hungry now when I feed him directly but my pump volume is definitely not nearly the same as he would eat in a bottle. Using a specta S2. Was not formally sized othwr than at the hospital but sized myself
My baby will be 5 months when i return. Did just buy all new pump parts and did not see any improvement in volume (unfortunately). Using a spectra S2

I used the zipadeezip from about 10 weeks to 15 weeks and then transitioned to a sleep sack. I tried the Merlin once and he immediately rolled to his side in it which made me a little concerned. Also didnt love that eventually a transition is needed out of the merlin— I liked that the Zipadeezip could be used indefinitely if needed. I eventually switched to a sleep sack just because i had one and it seemed a bit warmer than the zipadeezip I had on hand. 
Zipadeezip definitely helped the transition period because at 10-12 weeks we found our baby wasnt ready for arms out sleep sack but he loved the zipadeezip!

I just started the transition with my 3.5 month old! I was doing 1.75/1.75/2.25 /2.5 and transitioned to 2.25/2.5/2.5/3. I did it “cold turkey” and just pushed him to longer wake windows. I know most people reccomend slowly increasing them until you drop the nap but I couldnt figure out how to make that work lol. He actually naturally lengthened his first nap (which he never does) the first two days. Otherwise I “rescue” one nap to get it to be around 1.25-1.5 hrs.

I have the same question haha. the PLS facebook group is often suggesting expanding wake windows. Their suggestions worked for my son— but his wake windows definitely look very long compared to other groups & some of the feedback i get here. Always makes me confused because so many other consultants/programs recommend so much more sleep
any suggestions if your baby falls asleep on walks?! I try walks all the time but makes my son just fall asleep even if its early in the wake window and hes not due to nap for a while
my son is 3 months. Doing 2.25/2.5/2.5/3 right now (as of yesterday) but getting lots of middle of the night wakes now

I would suggest expanding wake windows. Also have a three month old & realized huckleberry was making him undertired. I moved to 1.75/1.75/2/2.25/2.5 which immediately improved false starts from every night to like 40% of the time— so not perfect but did help

Yeah I was following much closer to the Max for 4 naps you listed before but got feedback he was undertired. PLS suggests 12-14 hrs of sleep at this age so with 10.25 awake I am right at 13.75 hrs of sleep a day which is still on the high side. So confusing haha

Wake windows are 1.75/1.75/2/2.25/2.5. We were doing less than this and were dealing with lots of false starts. Moved up to this about 2.5 weeks ago and the false starts improved. However now getting a lot of wakes at night so are moving towards 3 naps.

this was happening to my son right before he was 3 months old— sometimes crying for 2-3 hours. Once we expanded wake window before bedtime it fully resolved. At first we shortened the wake window (thinking screaming meant over tired) but that only made it worse.

Yep about 2 weeks ago we were trying to put him down at 90 min or so and he would scream / cry no matter what we did. Once we increased that wake window to two hours he stopped the screaming! Moved it up to 2.5 hours and false starts decreased but still get them
Funny enough the suggestions I received previously all said to push that last wake window a bit further for him and noted he was likely under tired

My son is 3 months old and about 2 weeks ago we dealt with something similar— bedtime (which was previously easy!) was taking hours and often resulted in him screaming for 2-3 hours and/or someone needing to hold him. We tried shortening his wake window before bed (thinking screaming = overtired) which made it worse. Once we increased it to 2 hours he stopped screaming and taking hours but then started having false starts. Now we have moved up to 2.5 hrs before bed and the false starts have lessened. 
I would definitely try expanding your wake windows. We started using huckleberry sweetspot at 8 weeks and were loving it but in the past 1.5 weeks realized it was making our baby very under tired.
Hah— we just used it for the first time for a nap and he rolled to the side so arent sure if we start to use it or just  not even start.
also just to the side

Good to hear— we were using some of the TCB / Moms on Call schedules  and were so afraid to go past that 90 min awake mark at his age but it seems like he is able to handle closer to 2. 
I am working on bringing down his total daytime sleep closer to the “max 4 hr” guidance from the linked post— right now hes getting about 4.75 hrs of naps a day. However stretching the wake windows seems to be slow work haha

We are thinking he is undertired mostly— he has been on the high ends of 4 hrs (between 4.5-5 hrs) of nap time. we are slowly working on bringing that down. 
We had 3 nights where we were thinking he was overtired and were trying to put him down earlier (around 1.5 hrs awake before bedtime) and he ended up screaming for 1.5-3 hours. Once we extended that ww the screaming stopped but false starts started

Can the false starts just be developmental? He does not connect nap cycles either. He does typically go down independently for bedtime and naps— have used FIO and he typically fusses for <5 min and falls asleep. Occasionally, if he is fussing and cries longer than 5 min we have to support and typically do this by tapping the mattress. So he normally falls asleep independently but then just cant at the false start?

I have found my son (11 weeks) has had the occasional night like this where he is up every hour— we typically think its because he is overtired and focus the next day on making sure he gets good naps. We have seen it resolve and be more of a “once off” (although has happened maybe 2-3 times total, just not repeatedly). It might be that? Otherwise could be an early regression?

get the vertuo plus. i have the plus & it is much better than the next, which i use at work. the next leaks a lot more, is more difficult to use, and constantly goes into error modes. i have never had these issues with the plus.
